source: make a fun 3d shooter game where you czn unlock different weapons. make about 15 different weapons. Make skin boxes you czn opento get skins for different weapons and wrap boxes where you get cool textures (wraps) to apply to your guns. also make a lobby and matchmaking, a practice arena and dofferent gammodes

answers.ask: No setting was given - should the maps be modern military, sci-fi, or bright and cartoonish?
answers.answer: Use a bright, cartoonish shooter style so the weapons, skins, and wraps feel fun and readable.

answers.ask: Which space should be built first: the lobby, the practice range, or a match map?
answers.answer: Build the lobby first, since it is the hub for matchmaking, weapon unlocks, skin boxes, wrap boxes, and entering the practice arena.

answers.ask: Which game modes do you want - team deathmatch, free-for-all, objective modes?
answers.answer: Include team deathmatch and free-for-all first; keep objective modes out of the initial build.

- [author] theme — Q: No setting was given - should the maps be modern military, sci-fi, or bright and cartoonish? A: Use a bright, cartoonish shooter style so the weapons, skins, and wraps feel fun and readable.
- [author] shape — Q: Which space should be built first: the lobby, the practice range, or a match map? A: Build the lobby first, since it is the hub for matchmaking, weapon unlocks, skin boxes, wrap boxes, and entering the practice arena.
- [author] goal — Q: Which game modes do you want - team deathmatch, free-for-all, objective modes? A: Include team deathmatch and free-for-all first; keep objective modes out of the initial build.

## Enriched image prompt
Build the first scene as a bright, cartoonish 3D shooter lobby that acts as the hub for the rest of the game. Arrange a central gathering floor with a readable wall or display holding about 15 distinct weapons, plus clearly separated stations for opening skin boxes and wrap boxes. Place three prominent destination entrances around the hub: one to the practice arena, one for team deathmatch matchmaking, and one for free-for-all matchmaking. Use playful color coding and bold silhouettes so weapons, skins, wraps, and each destination remain easy to distinguish. Keep objective-mode entrances out of this initial lobby.

## Genre
Shooter is the sole genre; the lobby serves a weapon-based shooter even though the first rendered space is its hub.

## Shape and preset
Use `hub-portals`, named Portal Hub, from outside Shooter's usual shape set because the dominant space sends players to separate practice and match experiences. The preset is none: no Shooter preset describes the requested lobby-first hub.

## Config requirements
Use the shared `social-hub` option, taken from outside Shooter's shortlist, for the central lobby gathering space. Use `station-loadout` for the visible weapon display and interaction bench with about 15 distinct weapons. Use `teleporter-link` as separate-map portals for the practice arena, team deathmatch, and free-for-all; its route is `P4` here. The skin-box and wrap-box opening stations have no exact catalogue row, so retain them as scene-specific visible stations.

## Layout requirements
Place one `station-loadout` TriggerZone against the 15-weapon display in the lobby. Place three `teleporter-link` Teleporters on the three destination entrances: one paired to the practice arena, one to team deathmatch matchmaking, and one to free-for-all matchmaking. Place interaction TriggerZones on the separate skin-box and wrap-box stations. Do not place an objective-mode destination.

## Layout components
The lobby is the authoritative first map: one central social floor, a perimeter weapon wall or rack with about 15 readable weapon positions, one skin-box station, one wrap-box station, and three separated destination portals. The practice arena, team deathmatch map, and free-for-all map are subordinate separate-map destinations; the prompt does not describe their internal geometry, so their shapes remain open rather than invented. Keep clear walking space between every station and frame the lobby so all three exits are visible.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: render the bright lobby composition first and derive its top-down view, because the hub's visual hierarchy matters more than route topology and the destination maps are separate.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, driven by the need to read individual weapon and box stations inside a shared lobby. The theme is bright, cartoonish shooter. Use `P4` because the lobby connects to three separate maps; no other modifier is forced by the lobby geometry.
